11.grammar: Shahādatuhum is the subject (mubtadaʾ) of a nominal sentence, in the nominative case (-u ending on the construct: shahādatu-). The suffix -hum is possessive. Together: 'their testimony'.
11.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify; testimony, witnessing

12.meaning: And they will be questioned, and they shall be asked — wayusʾalūna is wa- (and) plus the imperfect passive yusʾalūna, meaning 'they will be asked/questioned'.

parts.en: imperfect passive verb, 3rd person masculine plural: they will be questioned, they will be asked

12.grammar: Wa- is the coordinating conjunction. Yusʾalūna is the Form I imperfect passive, third-person masculine plural, indicated by yu- prefix (with ḍamma), -ā- in the stem (passive vowel), and -ūna plural suffix. The passive voice means the questioning is done to them.
12.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, to question, to request

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
3.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

4.meaning: The Most Gracious / All-Merciful (al-Raḥmān) — a name of Allah from the root of mercy, in an intensive pattern denoting mercy that is vast, all-encompassing, and overflowing to all creation.
4.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'r', written al-raḥmān, said ar-raḥmān). An intensive noun-form expressing immense, overflowing mercy. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject, predicate, or name in apposition to such.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: We would not have worshipped them — ʿabadnāhum is the perfect verb ʿabadnā (we worshipped) plus -hum (them). In context with preceding mā (negation) it means 'we would not have worshipped them'.

parts.en: perfect verb, 1st person plural: we worshipped, we served
3rd person masculine plural object pronoun: them

6.grammar: ʿAbadnā is the Form I perfect verb, first-person plural (the suffix -nā = 'we'). The -hum is the object pronoun. In the broader sentence, mā before it negates the clause: 'we would not have worshipped them (had it not been for our fathers)'.
6.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, to be a servant of

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

9.meaning: About that, with that, by that — bidhālika is the preposition bi- (with, by, about) plus the demonstrative pronoun dhālika (that — masculine singular distal).
9.grammar: Bi- is a preposition governing the demonstrative dhālika (which doesn't inflect for case; it is invariable). The phrase functions as an adverbial: 'about/concerning that thing'.
9.root: — (bi is a particle; dhā-lika is a demonstrative; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
10.root: — (preposition)

11.meaning: Knowledge — ʿil'm is a verbal noun meaning knowledge, learning, certainty of fact. In the genitive indefinite it follows a preposition or a construct noun.

parts.en: noun, indefinite genitive: knowledge, certainty, learning

11.grammar: ʿIl'min is the genitive (kasra -in tanwīn) of ʿilm. The genitive here follows a preposition (e.g., min 'from' or bi 'about') or is part of a negative statement about someone's knowledge.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, to have knowledge of; knowledge

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
13.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: They guess, conjecture, or speak from mere estimation; from a verb meaning to surmise or speak falsely without sound basis.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I) with the ya- prefix. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood, used for an ongoing or habitual statement.
15.root: خ-ر-ص (kh-r-ṣ) — to conjecture, estimate, speak by guesswork

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: We gave them / We granted them; a completed act of bestowing or providing, done by a "we" subject and directed to a group as recipients.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning "to give/grant." The attached -nā marks the subject as "we" (the doer), and the attached -hum marks "them" as the recipients/object. The form states a completed action.
2.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (in this form) to bring, give, grant

3.meaning: 'A writing / a prescribed decree' — that which is written down; by extension a fixed ordinance, an appointed term, or a binding decree.
3.grammar: An indefinite noun in the accusative case: the -an ending (the 'an' sound with nunation) marks the object of a verb or a related role, and signals an indefinite 'a writing/decree'. The pattern 'kitāb' is the verbal noun denoting a written thing.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: Before; the period or point in time (or place) prior to something. With the attached pronoun it means 'before it / before him', pointing to what came earlier.
5.grammar: An adverb/noun of time meaning 'before', functioning here as something governed in the genitive (the -i ending), as it regularly follows a preposition such as 'from'. The attached -hi means 'it / him' ('before it'); the vowel of the pronoun is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows the -i ending.
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede; front, priorness

6.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
6.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

7.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: Holding fast, clinging firmly — mustamsikūna is the Form X active participle plural of istamasaka meaning to hold on firmly, to cling to, to grasp tightly.

parts.en: active participle plural (Form X), nominative: those who hold fast, those who cling firmly

8.grammar: Mustamsikūna is the Form X (istafʿala pattern) active participle in the masculine plural nominative (-ūna ending). Form X often implies seeking or striving toward the root meaning: 'striving to hold firm'. Functions as a predicate: 'they are those who hold fast'.
8.root: م-س-ك (m-s-k) — to hold, grasp; Form X: to hold on firmly, to cling to

1.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

2.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

3.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
3.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

4.meaning: 'We found / came upon / discovered' — to find something, either by encountering it or by determining it to be in a certain state.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb with the '-nā' ending meaning 'we'. So it means 'we found' or 'we came upon'. The '-nā' suffix attached to the past-tense stem marks the doers as a 'we' (first-person plural).
4.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to discover

5.meaning: 'Our fathers / forefathers / ancestors.' The plural of 'father,' denoting forebears and the line of those who came before, with the attached 'our' marking them as one's own ancestry.
5.grammar: A plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessive -nā ('our'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used to mark the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or certain adverbial roles.
5.root: أ-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — father, fatherhood

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
6.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').
6.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
7.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.
7.root: ء-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — community, way, intent

8.meaning: "and indeed we" — the connective "and" plus the emphasis particle inna ("truly, indeed") with the attached subject "we."
8.grammar: The particle inna strongly affirms the statement that follows ("it is certainly the case that…"). The attached subject pronoun is -nā ("we"); its ن is assimilated into the doubled نّ of inna, so only the long vowel ا is written, but the morpheme is still nā. The leading wa- is the connective "and." Inna also puts its noun into the accusative state.

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
9.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').
9.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: Their footsteps, their traces, their path — āthārihim is the plural of athar (trace, mark, footstep, legacy) plus -him (their, third person masculine plural genitive).

parts.en: plural noun, genitive construct: traces, footsteps, marks, legacy
3rd person masculine plural genitive pronoun: their

10.grammar: Āthāri is the genitive (broken) plural of athar, in construct state before the pronoun suffix. The -i ending is genitive, showing it follows a preposition or is the second term of an iḍāfa. -Him is the attached genitive plural pronoun.
10.root: أ-ث-ر (ʾ-th-r) — trace, mark, footstep; to follow in the footsteps of

11.meaning: Those who are rightly guided — people who have found and follow the correct path. It describes a plural group in that guided state.
11.grammar: An active participle of a reflexive pattern (one who has accepted/found guidance for himself), in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative (subject) form, describing a group as 'rightly guided ones'.
11.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, be rightly guided

1.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
3.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
5.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
6.root: — (particle)

7.meaning: a town / a settlement — an inhabited place such as a village or city; a gathering of dwellings.
7.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -in ending carries two signals at once: the genitive case (used after prepositions or to link to a preceding word, '… of …') and the indefinite 'a/an' (no definite article), conveying 'a town'.
7.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather; a settled place

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: One who warns; a giver of warning who alerts people to danger or coming consequences. It can name a person (a warner) or function as an intensive description (one who warns earnestly).
9.grammar: An active-participle-like noun on the faʿīl pattern, meaning 'a warner.' The ending -in is indefinite ('a warner,' not 'the warner') and genitive, the case used after a preposition or when a noun is linked to a preceding noun as a possessor or specifier.
9.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, to caution

10.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
10.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
10.root: — (particle)

11.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
11.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

12.meaning: The wealthy/affluent ones of it, its elite — mutrafūhā is the plural active participle of atrafa (to give luxury to, to make comfortable) plus -hā (its/her, feminine pronoun).

parts.en: active participle plural (Form IV), construct nominative: the ones given luxury, the affluent ones
3rd person feminine singular pronoun: its, her

12.grammar: Mutrafū is the Form IV active participle masculine plural in the construct nominative (dropping the -na of -ūna when in construct). The Form IV atrafa means 'to give luxury/affluence to someone'. The suffix -hā refers to the town or city (feminine in Arabic).
12.root: ت-ر-ف (t-r-f) — to live in luxury, to be affluent; Form IV: to make affluent, to give ease/luxury to

13.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
13.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

14.meaning: 'We found / came upon / discovered' — to find something, either by encountering it or by determining it to be in a certain state.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb with the '-nā' ending meaning 'we'. So it means 'we found' or 'we came upon'. The '-nā' suffix attached to the past-tense stem marks the doers as a 'we' (first-person plural).
14.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to discover

15.meaning: 'Our fathers / forefathers / ancestors.' The plural of 'father,' denoting forebears and the line of those who came before, with the attached 'our' marking them as one's own ancestry.
15.grammar: A plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessive -nā ('our'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used to mark the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or certain adverbial roles.

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
16.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

17.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
17.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

18.meaning: "and indeed we" — the connective "and" plus the emphasis particle inna ("truly, indeed") with the attached subject "we."
18.grammar: The particle inna strongly affirms the statement that follows ("it is certainly the case that…"). The attached subject pronoun is -nā ("we"); its ن is assimilated into the doubled نّ of inna, so only the long vowel ا is written, but the morpheme is still nā. The leading wa- is the connective "and." Inna also puts its noun into the accusative state.

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
19.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

20.meaning: Their footsteps, their traces, their path — āthārihim is the plural of athar (trace, mark, footstep, legacy) plus -him (their, third person masculine plural genitive).

parts.en: plural noun, genitive construct: traces, footsteps, marks, legacy
3rd person masculine plural genitive pronoun: their

20.grammar: Āthāri is the genitive (broken) plural of athar, in construct state before the pronoun suffix. The -i ending is genitive, showing it follows a preposition or is the second term of an iḍāfa. -Him is the attached genitive plural pronoun.
20.root: أ-ث-ر (ʾ-th-r) — trace, mark, footstep; to follow in the footsteps of

21.meaning: (Are) following, imitating — muqtadūna is the Form VIII active participle plural of iqtadā meaning to follow, to imitate, to pattern oneself after someone.

parts.en: active participle plural (Form VIII), nominative: those who follow, those who imitate

21.grammar: Muqtadūna is the Form VIII (iftaʿala) active participle, masculine plural nominative (-ūna). Form VIII of q-d-w/y means 'to follow, to take as an example'. Functions as a predicate or description.
21.root: ق-د-و/ي (q-d-w/y) — to lead; Form VIII: to follow, to imitate, to pattern after

1.meaning: He said / he spoke — a simple past-tense statement of someone uttering words.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The final -a is the standard ending for 'he/it' having done something. The long ā in the stem comes from an original middle root-letter (w) that has shifted to ā in this form.

2.meaning: A clustered opener used to challenge or press a point: roughly 'even if…?' / 'what, even though…?' It joins a questioning hamza ('really?'), the connector 'wa' (and), and 'law' (if/though), introducing a hypothetical that is being questioned or objected to.
2.grammar: A combination of particles: the question-marker a- (turning the phrase into a rhetorical challenge), the conjunction wa- ('and/even'), and the conditional law ('if/though'), which introduces a hypothetical condition. Being particles, none of them take case endings.

3.meaning: I have come to you — a completed act of arriving or bringing oneself, directed toward a group of addressees.
3.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb. The -tu ending means 'I' did the action; the -kum suffix is the object 'you (all)'. So the form conveys 'I came / have come to you-plural', presenting the arrival as already accomplished.

4.meaning: Better guidance, more rightly guided — bi-ahdā is the preposition bi- plus ahdā, the comparative/superlative Form (af'al) of hudā/hadā meaning more guided or better at guiding.

parts.en: elative adjective (comparative/superlative): better guided, more guiding

4.grammar: Bi- is a preposition governing the noun. Ahdā is the af'al pattern (elative) of the root h-d-y, meaning 'more guided / better guidance'. The final alif (maqṣūra) is uninflected in the elative.
4.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to show the right way; guidance

5.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
5.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

6.meaning: You found / came upon — to discover, encounter, or find something to be in a certain state, expressed as a completed past act by 'you all'.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with the suffix '-tum', the masculine plural subject marker 'you all'. The doubled 't' arises as the stem's final 'd' assimilates into the suffix's 't'. The past tense presents the finding as completed.
6.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find/come upon; to experience

7.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
7.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

8.meaning: Fathers, forefathers, ancestors — male parents, and by extension the line of forebears.
8.grammar: A plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessive pronoun '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-a' between the noun and the pronoun marks the accusative case (typically a direct object); '-kum' adds the possessor 'of you all' (ābāʾakum).
8.root: ء-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — father, fatherhood

9.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
9.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

10.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
10.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
11.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
11.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

12.meaning: 'You have been sent / were sent.' The verb is passive: it speaks of being dispatched or commissioned by someone else, as messengers are sent with a charge. The form addresses a group ('you all').
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice, built on the causative 'sending' form ('to be sent / dispatched'). The attached -tum ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), here the ones receiving the action. The past tense presents the sending as already accomplished.

13.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
13.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

14.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers: those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle names people characterized by ungrateful rejection of what should be acknowledged.
14.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate (as opposed to -īna for object/genitive).
14.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: 'So we took retribution / we exacted justice.' The verb means to avenge, to punish in just recompense, to exact a penalty for a wrong. It carries the sense of a measured, deserved requital rather than random anger.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the reflexive/intensive (Form VIII) pattern, in the 'we' person, with a connective prefix. The fa- means 'so / then,' marking a consequence. The stem intaqam- is completed (past) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers ('we exacted retribution'). The Form VIII pattern (with the infixed -t-) gives the sense of taking the act fully upon oneself.
1.root: ن-ق-م (n-q-m) — to avenge, exact retribution, punish a wrong

2.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with pronoun, no root)

3.meaning: So look! / then observe! — a command to one person to look at, consider, and reflect upon something.
3.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you', prefixed by fa- ('so/then'), which links it as a consequence of what precedes. The verb urges one to look and reflect: 'so look!' / 'then consider!'
3.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

4.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
4.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

5.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

5.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

6.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
6.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
6.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

7.meaning: Of the deniers, of those who reject — al-mukadhibīna is the masculine plural oblique (genitive/accusative) of the Form II active participle mukadhhib meaning one who denies, rejects, or calls something a lie.

parts.en: active participle plural (Form II), definite oblique: the deniers, those who reject the truth

7.grammar: Al-mukadhibīna is the masculine plural oblique (genitive/accusative) of the Form II active participle. The -īna ending marks the masculine plural oblique. Form II (kadhhaba) means 'to call a liar / to deny emphatically'.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; Form II: to deny, to call a liar, to reject as false

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

3.meaning: A proper noun: Abraham (Ibrāhīm), the patriarch and prophet, exalted as an upright monotheist and 'friend of Allah'.
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. Because it is a foreign proper name, it is 'diptote' — it does not take the indefinite 'n' sound (tanwīn) that ordinary nouns would.

4.meaning: To / for his father — the noun 'father' attached to a possessive 'his' and preceded by the preposition 'to/for.'
4.grammar: Preposition + noun + possessive pronoun. The li- prefix means 'to' or 'for.' 'Father' is one of a small group of nouns that show case with a long vowel: the -ī here reflects the genitive required after the preposition. The attached -hi means 'his' (its 'i' vowel harmonizes after the preceding -ī).

5.meaning: And his people / his folk / his kinfolk — the community or nation to which a person belongs, plus 'his.'
5.grammar: A noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and') and carrying the possessive -hi ('his'). The -i ending is genitive; here it appears because of the attached possessive pronoun (a noun linked to a following possessor stands in the genitive). Qawm denotes a people, tribe, or community.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people who stand together

6.meaning: 'Indeed I / truly, as for me' — an emphatic opening particle (inna, 'indeed/truly') fused with an attached 'I.' It introduces a statement about oneself with stress and certainty.
6.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed, truly') with the attached pronoun -ī ('I/me'), joined by a buffer -n- (giving -nanī). Inna stresses and affirms the sentence it opens. The final -ī suffix is the first-person singular ('I'), the thing inna is making a statement about.
6.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: Disassociated, free of, absolved — barāʾun is the verbal noun/noun of barāʾa, meaning to be free of, to disavow, to be absolved of responsibility for something. Here it functions as a predicate: 'I am free of / I disavow'.

parts.en: noun (verbal noun form), indefinite nominative: disavowal, freedom from, absolution

7.grammar: Barāʾun is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used predicatively in the nominative indefinite (-un tanwīn). It means 'one who is/I am free from / disassociated'. The hamza ending is part of the root.
7.root: ب-ر-أ (b-r-ʾ) — to be free of, to be innocent of, to disavow

8.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
8.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

9.meaning: You worship (Him) — to serve, devote oneself to, and submit in obedient adoration to a deity. The verb conveys total devotion: not merely outward ritual but the humble servitude a worshipper owes to the One worshipped.
9.grammar: Present/future-tense verb addressed to a group of males ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks second person ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural subjects and the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact, 'you do/will worship'), as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form which would drop the final -na.
9.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He originated me' / 'He brought me into being' — the act of creating something new from nothing, bringing it into existence for the first time, with the attached 'me' as its object.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he originated/created.' The doer 'he' (third-person masculine singular) is unmarked — carried by the bare verb form itself with no added personal suffix; the final '-a' is simply the base vowel on the last root letter. The attached '-nī' is the object pronoun 'me' (its 'n' is a connecting sound between verb and pronoun). So the whole means 'He originated me.'
3.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to originate, bring into being, split forth into existence

4.meaning: A cluster of three elements: a connective 'so/then', the emphasis particle 'inna' that strongly affirms a statement ('indeed, truly'), and 'he/it'. Together: 'so indeed he / then truly it'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connecting particle showing sequence or consequence ('so, then'). 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the sentence that follows and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached 'hu' is that pronoun, 'he/it', here serving as the subject being emphasized.

5.meaning: Will guide me — sayahdīni is sa- (future marker) plus yahdīni, the imperfect verb of hadā (to guide) in the third-person masculine singular with the first-person singular object suffix -nī (-i after the verb's final vowel drops -n before attaching).

parts.en: imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular: he guides, will guide

5.grammar: Sa- marks the near/definite future. Yahdīni is a defective (naqs) root verb; the final yāʾ represents the long vowel ī of the imperfect, and -ni is the first-person singular object suffix (the nūn of wiqāya protects the vowel).
5.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to show the path; guidance

1.meaning: And He made it, and he placed it — wajaʿalahā is wa- (and) + jaʿala (perfect verb: he made/placed/rendered) + -hā (feminine singular object: it/her).

parts.en: perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular: he made, he placed, he rendered
3rd person feminine singular object pronoun: it, her

1.grammar: Wa- coordinates with the preceding clause. Jaʿala is the Form I perfect verb, 3rd masculine singular. The suffix -hā is the feminine singular object pronoun referring to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
1.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to place, to render, to put into a state

2.meaning: A word; an utterance or saying — a single meaningful unit of speech, and by extension a statement, expression, or pronouncement.
2.grammar: A feminine noun (its -a / tāʾ marbūṭa is the feminine marker). The final -an written over the tāʾ (tanwīn fatḥa, sounded '-tan') marks the indefinite accusative — the case for an object, or for the noun specified after verbs of the 'how grave is…' type.
2.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — to speak; word, speech

3.meaning: Remaining, lasting, enduring — bāqiyatan is the feminine accusative of bāqiya, the active participle of baqiya meaning to remain, to endure, to persist.

parts.en: active participle, feminine indefinite accusative: remaining, lasting, enduring

3.grammar: Bāqiyatan is the feminine form of the active participle bāqin, in the indefinite accusative (-tan ending with tanwīn fatḥa). The feminine agrees with a feminine noun it describes (e.g., a word/legacy that remains).
3.root: ب-ق-ي (b-q-y) — to remain, to endure, to persist; that which remains

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: His descendants, his progeny, those who came after him — ʿaqibihi is ʿaqib (that which follows, heel, outcome, descendants) plus -hi (his). It denotes those who came in his wake or his successors.

parts.en: noun, genitive construct: heel; descendants, successors, that which follows

5.grammar: ʿAqibi is in the genitive case (kasra -i ending) as the first term of an iḍāfa with the pronoun -hi. It can mean 'in his wake', 'after him', or 'his descendants/posterity'. The word ʿaqib literally means 'heel' and by extension 'those who follow after'.
5.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — heel; to follow after, to succeed; descendants, outcome

6.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

6.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
6.root: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

7.meaning: To return, go back, or turn back — to come back to a place, state, or point of origin. Used of a group: 'they return / come back'.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they return'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna 'indicative' ending appears when nothing precedes the verb to shorten it.
7.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — returning, going back, repetition

1.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

2.meaning: I gave enjoyment, I let them enjoy — mattaʿtu is the Form II perfect verb of mattaʿa (to give enjoyment/benefit to), first-person singular, meaning 'I gave them enjoyment / I let them benefit'.

parts.en: perfect verb (Form II), 1st person singular: I gave enjoyment, I provided benefit to

2.grammar: Mattaʿtu is Form II (faʿʿala — intensive/causative), the perfect tense with the first-person singular suffix -tu. Form II of m-t-ʿ means to give material enjoyment or benefit to someone. The -tu suffix = 'I' as subject.
2.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, to benefit; Form II: to give enjoyment/benefit to

3.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
3.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

4.meaning: 'And their fathers / forefathers' — the plural of 'father' with 'their' attached, referring to the ancestors of a group, joined with 'and.'
4.grammar: Plural noun 'fathers/forefathers' with the possessive 'their' (-hum). The -a ending marks the accusative (object) state, typically the object of a verb or the subject of certain particles. It often broadens to mean ancestors generally.

5.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
5.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: It came to them / he came to them: a completed act of arriving or coming, with the recipients ('them') built into the word.

parts.en: final vowel of the past-tense base (he/it)

6.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it … '), expressing a completed action. In this form the 'he/it' subject carries no added suffix — the -a is simply the final vowel resting on the last root letter of the base, not a person marker. The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word.
6.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

7.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
7.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
7.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

8.meaning: And a Messenger — warasūlun is wa- (and) plus rasūl (messenger, prophet, envoy) in the nominative indefinite.

parts.en: noun, nominative indefinite: messenger, envoy, prophet

8.grammar: Wa- is the coordinating conjunction. Rasūlun is a masculine noun in the nominative case (ḍamma -un tanwīn), functioning as a subject or additional predicate. Rasūl is from the same root as irsāl (sending) and refers to one sent with a divine message.
8.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; messenger, envoy, prophet

9.meaning: Clear, plain, and self-evident; that which makes things manifest. The form carries an active sense: not merely 'clear in itself' but 'making clear,' something that openly displays its nature and leaves no ambiguity.
9.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) on the form mufʿil, meaning 'one who/that which makes [something] clear.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness, clarity

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: It came to them / he came to them: a completed act of arriving or coming, with the recipients ('them') built into the word.

parts.en: final vowel of the past-tense base (he/it)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it … '), expressing a completed action. In this form the 'he/it' subject carries no added suffix — the -a is simply the final vowel resting on the last root letter of the base, not a person marker. The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word.
2.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

3.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
3.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

4.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

5.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
5.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

6.meaning: Magic / sorcery — the working of illusions or hidden powers to deceive perception or affect people; by extension, anything dazzling that distorts how things truly are.
6.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a/some magic') and in the nominative case — the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or after the verb 'to be'.
6.root: س-ح-ر (s-ḥ-r) — magic, enchantment, beguiling

7.meaning: "and indeed we" — the connective "and" plus the emphasis particle inna ("truly, indeed") with the attached subject "we."
7.grammar: The particle inna strongly affirms the statement that follows ("it is certainly the case that…"). The attached subject pronoun is -nā ("we"); its ن is assimilated into the doubled نّ of inna, so only the long vowel ا is written, but the morpheme is still nā. The leading wa- is the connective "and." Inna also puts its noun into the accusative state.

8.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

9.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers: those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle names people characterized by ungrateful rejection of what should be acknowledged.
9.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate (as opposed to -īna for object/genitive).
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
2.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

3.meaning: A past-tense passive verb meaning 'it was sent down / caused to descend' — something made to come down (typically revelation), with an intensive nuance of being sent down gradually or fully.
3.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) passive verb of Form II (the doubled-middle pattern, which adds intensity or gradualness), 3rd-person masculine singular. The vowel shape 'nuzzila' (u–i) marks it as passive: the subject is the thing acted upon, with the doer unnamed ('it was sent down'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending.
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (sending down)

4.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
4.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

5.meaning: The Qur'ān — literally 'the Recitation' or 'that which is read aloud'; the name of the revealed Scripture, understood as something recited.
5.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the recitation') used as a proper name. The final -u is the nominative case, the ending that typically marks the subject or the thing being identified.
5.root: ق-ر-ا (q-r-ʾ) — to read, recite, gather together

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

7.meaning: A man — a single adult male human being, indefinite ('a man / some man').
7.grammar: A noun with the -in (indefinite genitive) ending, the case that typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of a man') or follows a preposition. The tanwīn (-in) signals it is indefinite ('a man / a certain man').
7.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: The two towns, the two cities — al-qaryatayni is the dual genitive of qarya (town, village, city). 'The two towns' refers to Mecca and Taif in the context of the surah.

parts.en: dual noun, definite genitive: the two towns, the two cities

9.grammar: Al-qaryatayni is the dual genitive form (-ayni ending) of qarya (town), preceded by the definite article. The dual genitive -ayni is used when the noun follows a preposition or is governed by a preceding noun/verb.
9.root: ق-ر-ي/و (q-r-y/w) — to settle; village, town, city

10.meaning: An adjective meaning 'great', 'immense', 'mighty', or 'tremendous' — vast in size, importance, or gravity; used of things weighty and momentous.
10.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying a strong, established quality), carrying the genitive indefinite '-in' (tanwīn) ending. The genitive case typically appears after a preposition or when describing/qualifying a preceding genitive noun.
10.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense; (literally) bone, hence weightiness

1.meaning: A question word fused with a pronoun: 'Are they …?' The a- is the particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, and -hum is the pronoun 'they,' so together it opens an inquiry about a masculine plural group.
1.grammar: An interrogative particle a- ('?') prefixed to the detached pronoun hum ('they'). It introduces a yes/no question whose subject is 'they,' as in 'Are they …?' The pronoun itself does not change form for case.

2.meaning: They distribute, they divide up — yaqsimūna is the third-person masculine plural imperfect of qasama meaning to divide, distribute, or apportion.

parts.en: imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural: they distribute, they divide up, they apportion

2.grammar: The ya- prefix marks third person (masculine). The -ūna ending is the nominative plural suffix for the imperfect verb. Qasama (Form I) means to divide or distribute something among people.
2.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to divide, distribute, apportion; an oath

3.meaning: Mercy: tender compassion, lovingkindness, and the active will to relieve and show favor. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's boundless, gracious mercy.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The feminine ending tā' marbūṭa carries the vowel -a, which here marks the accusative case: the noun is the direct object of a verb ('they hope for mercy'). The accusative is the case used for the object of an action.

4.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
4.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

5.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
5.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

6.meaning: We distribute, We divide — qasamnā is the first-person plural perfect of qasama meaning to divide or distribute. The first-person plural reflects divine majesty (naḥnu).

parts.en: perfect verb, 1st person plural: We divided, We distributed, We apportioned

6.grammar: Qasamnā is the Form I perfect, first-person plural (the -nā suffix = 'we'). It is the majestic plural used by Allah in the Qur'an. The verb expresses a completed act of distribution.
6.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to divide, distribute, apportion; share, portion

7.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
7.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

8.meaning: Their livelihood, their means of sustenance — maʿīshatahum is maʿīsha (livelihood, sustenance, means of living) plus -hum (their).

parts.en: noun (verbal noun pattern), accusative construct: livelihood, living, sustenance

8.grammar: Maʿīshata is the accusative construct of maʿīsha (a verbal noun from ʿāsha 'to live'). It functions as the object of a verb or the first term of an iḍāfa with -hum. The accusative -a ending plus construct state (no tanwīn).
8.root: ع-ي-ش (ʿ-y-sh) — to live; livelihood, means of sustenance

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
10.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.
10.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, being alive, living

11.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
11.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

12.meaning: "And We raised / lifted up" — to raise, lift, or elevate something physically or in rank. The form carries a 'we' subject, opened by the conjunction 'and'.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached subject suffix '-nā' ('we'), marking a completed action done by a group (or the majestic 'We'). Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.

13.meaning: "some of them / a part of them" — the word baʿḍ means 'a portion/some', and with the attached pronoun it means 'some of them', singling out part of a group.
13.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive/partitive pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or the second term of certain constructions. The suffix -hum means 'them' (third-person masculine plural).

14.meaning: 'Above / over / on top of.' An adverb of place meaning the higher position relative to something else; it can also mean 'superior to' or 'beyond.'
14.grammar: An adverb of place that is normally attached to a following noun ('above …'). Its fixed -a ending is the form such place-words take when they govern the noun that follows them.
14.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, surpass, exceed

15.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
15.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
15.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

16.meaning: "degrees / ranks / levels / steps" — the plural of daraja, a step or grade in an ascending scale; it denotes ranks, levels, or stages of elevation.
16.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -in (with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('degrees, ranks') and in the accusative/genitive case — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
16.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — step, grade, to ascend by degrees

17.meaning: So that (he/one) may take — liyattakhidha is li- (purpose: in order to) plus yattakhidha, the Form VIII jussive/subjunctive of akhadha meaning to take something as (a companion, servant, etc.).

parts.en: purpose particle: so that, in order to
Form VIII jussive/subjunctive, 3rd person masculine singular: he may take (as)

17.grammar: Li- governs the subjunctive (majzūm/manṣūb) mood. Yattakhidha is the Form VIII (ittakhadha — to take for oneself) in the jussive third-person masculine singular, marked by the -a ending (subjunctive). Used to express purpose.
17.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take; Form VIII: to take as, to adopt, to make into

18.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
18.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
18.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

19.meaning: Some, a part, or one of a group — 'another' when paired with 'one'. It singles out an unspecified portion or member set against the rest.

parts.en: some / a part / one (of a group)

19.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part / some'. The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case used for a direct object. Paired with baʿḍ ('another'), it builds the sense 'one another / each other'.
19.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some of a whole

20.meaning: For service, as a subject of mockery / subservience — sukh'riyyan is the indefinite accusative of sukhrī/sukhrayyan, meaning subjected to servitude, made subservient, or used for mockery/service.

parts.en: noun/adjective, indefinite accusative: subject to service, subservient; also: object of ridicule

20.grammar: Sukh'riyyan is in the indefinite accusative (-an tanwīn) and functions as a ḥāl (circumstantial: 'as something subservient') or an object. The doubled yāʾ (nisba-like form) derives from sukhr (servitude/mockery).
20.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to subjugate, press into service; to mock; servitude

21.meaning: But the Mercy — waraḥmatu is wa- (but/and) plus raḥmat (mercy, compassion) in the nominative construct. Here 'the Mercy of your Lord' contrasts with worldly goods.

parts.en: feminine noun, nominative construct: mercy, compassion

21.grammar: Waraḥmatu: wa- is the coordinating/contrastive conjunction. Raḥmatu is the feminine noun in the nominative (-u ending) in construct state (muḍāf, first of iḍāfa). Without tanwīn because it is followed by a genitive complement ('of your Lord').
21.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion; to be merciful

22.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
22.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
22.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

23.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
23.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
23.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

24.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
24.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

25.meaning: They gather, collect, amass, or heap up — the ongoing accumulating of things (such as wealth).
25.grammar: A present/future Form I verb. The ya- prefix plus the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject doing the action now or habitually, 'they gather.' The full -ūna (with final nūn) is the indicative form, used for a plain statement (not negated or subordinated).
25.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, bring together

1.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

1.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
2.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
2.root: — (particle; no root)

3.meaning: '(That) He be / there be' — a form of the core verb 'to be/become', expressing existence or a state of being.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is/becomes' or 'there is'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after certain particles (e.g. 'that', 'so that', 'in order to') and giving the sense of a dependent or hoped-for action.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

4.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
4.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
4.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

5.meaning: "a community / a nation / a people" — a single group bound together as one body, typically by shared faith, way of life, or leadership; 'umma' is a collective people united around something.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun, indefinite ('a community'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain verbs of making/becoming; the final alif is the written seat of this ending.
5.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward, intend; a community/leadership (cf. imām)

6.meaning: One, single, sole — the feminine form of the word for 'one', denoting unity and singleness, that there is just one of something with no second alongside it.
6.grammar: A feminine singular adjective/numeral meaning 'one'. The taa marbuuta makes it agree with a feminine noun. The final -an (accusative, with tanwin) marks it as indefinite and as describing or counting an accusative noun. The opening wa- is a separate connecting particle ('and').
6.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — to be one, single, unique

7.meaning: We would have made, We would have appointed — lajaʿalnā is the emphatic la- plus jaʿalnā (perfect, first-person plural: we made/appointed). In a conditional sentence: 'We would have made...'.

parts.en: emphatic lām (lām al-jawāb): surely, would have
perfect verb, 1st person plural: We made, We appointed, We rendered

7.grammar: La- here is the lām of the conditional apodosis (jawāb al-law/lawlā), indicating the consequence: 'We would surely have made'. JaʿalnĀ is the first-person plural perfect with the -nā suffix.
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, cause to be

8.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
8.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

9.meaning: He disbelieves, he is ungrateful — yakfuru is the third-person masculine singular imperfect of kafara meaning to disbelieve or to be ungrateful.

parts.en: imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular: he disbelieves, is ungrateful, covers the truth

9.grammar: Yakfuru is the Form I imperfect, third-person masculine singular (ya- prefix + -u nominative ending). It can describe an ongoing or habitual action: 'he disbelieves / is in a state of ingratitude'.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, to be ungrateful, to disbelieve

10.meaning: By the All-Merciful — al-Raḥmān, a name of Allah denoting boundless, all-embracing mercy that overflows to the whole of creation; a quality so intense it functions almost as a proper name.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, in') joined to the definite name al-Raḥmān. The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition. The name follows an intensive pattern signifying mercy that is vast, overflowing, and all-encompassing.
10.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, tender care

11.meaning: For their houses — libuyūtihim is li- (preposition: for) plus buyūt (houses, plural of bayt) plus -him (their).

parts.en: 3rd person masculine plural genitive pronoun: their

11.grammar: Li- governs the genitive. Buyūtihim is the genitive plural of bayt with the possessive pronoun -him. The broken plural buyūt (houses) is in the genitive case following the preposition.
11.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — house, home; to spend the night

12.meaning: Roofs, ceilings — suqufan is the plural of saqf (roof, ceiling, upper covering). In the indefinite accusative it refers to the roofs of houses.

parts.en: plural noun, indefinite accusative: roofs, ceilings

12.grammar: Suqufan is the broken plural of saqf in the indefinite accusative (-an tanwīn). It functions as the object of a verb of making or as a noun in apposition describing what would be given.
12.root: س-ق-ف (s-q-f) — roof, ceiling; to cover with a roof

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

14.meaning: Silver — fiḍḍatin is the noun fiḍḍa (silver) in the indefinite genitive. A precious metal used for ornamentation and currency.
