7.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, guard; Form VIII: to guard oneself (from Allah's displeasure); taqwā = God-fearing piety

1.meaning: O My servants — yāʿibādi is yā (vocative: O!) plus ʿibādi (my servants, genitive construct of ʿibād + first-person singular possessive -ī/-i).

parts.en: plural noun, genitive construct: servants, worshippers (of mine)

1.grammar: Yā is the vocative. ʿIbādi is the broken plural of ʿabd in the genitive (the -ī possessive suffix replaces the case ending: ʿibādu-ī → ʿibādī → ʿibādi). The possessive is first-person singular (Allah speaking). Together: 'O My servants'.
1.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve; servant, slave

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: 'Fear' — a state of being afraid, dread, or alarm; apprehension of something harmful or threatening.
3.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a fear' or simply 'fear' — and the nominative typically signals the doer or subject of a sentence, or the subject of an existential statement ('there is fear').

4.meaning: 'Upon / over you (plural)' — the preposition 'on, over, upon' with an attached 'you all' pronoun, indicating something coming onto or directed at a group.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -kum addresses a group ('you all'); the final -u (kumu) is a connecting helper-vowel easing the link into a following word that starts with the definite article. The preposition conveys 'on' or 'over'.

5.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
5.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
5.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
7.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

8.meaning: You grieve: a present-tense verb of feeling sorrow, sadness, or grief over loss or distress. It denotes inner mourning and heaviness of heart.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the -na also signals the indicative mood, used for plain statements (and is dropped when a particle of negation or command governs the verb).
8.root: ح-ز-ن (ḥ-z-n) — grief, sorrow, sadness

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

3.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
3.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

4.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

5.meaning: Those who submit — people who surrender themselves to Allah; 'Muslims,' i.e. ones fully yielded in obedience and peace to the divine will. From the verb meaning to submit/surrender wholly.
5.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' of the verb 'to submit'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — 'submitting ones,' used when the word is an object or follows a preposition.
5.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, soundness, submission

1.meaning: Enter! / go in!: a command verb directing the addressees to go into a place. It is the imperative of the verb 'to enter.'
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs a masculine plural 'you' — a command addressed to a group ('enter, all of you'). The opening vowel (alif) is a helping vowel needed to begin pronunciation of the command.

2.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — the place of lush, shaded greenery promised as the abode of bliss; literally a garden whose foliage covers the ground.
2.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. 'janna' is a feminine noun (the tā marbūṭa ending). The final -a is accusative, the form typically marking a word as the object of a verb or, with place-nouns, the destination/location toward which an action occurs.
2.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide

3.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
3.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

4.meaning: Spouses — husbands or wives; mates and partners. The word denotes one of a pair, the marriage partner who completes the other.
4.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. The word is a plural noun ('spouses, mates') with the attached possessive '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-u' before the pronoun marks the nominative case — typically the subject or predicate of a sentence; '-kum' supplies the possessor 'of you all' (azwājukum).
4.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pair, mate, spouse, to join two as a couple

5.meaning: Will be delighted, will be made joyful — tuḥbarūna is the imperfect passive, second-person masculine plural of ḥabara meaning to make happy, to delight, to gladden.

parts.en: imperfect passive verb, 2nd person masculine plural: you will be delighted, you will be made joyful

5.grammar: Tuḥbarūna is the Form I imperfect passive (tu- prefix with ḍamma, -a on the root middle = passive vowel pattern), second-person masculine plural (-ūna nominative). Passive: the delight is brought to you as a gift.
5.root: ح-ب-ر (ḥ-b-r) — to delight, to make happy, to bring joy; delight

1.meaning: Will be passed around, will be circulated — yuṭāfu is the imperfect passive of ṭāfa (to go around, to circumambulate) Form I or Form IV. Third-person masculine singular passive: 'it will be circulated/passed around'.

parts.en: imperfect passive verb, 3rd person masculine singular: it will be circulated, passed around

1.grammar: Yuṭāfu is the Form I imperfect passive (yu- ḍamma prefix, -ā- in stem for passive), third-person masculine singular. The passive voice means the subject (dishes) are circulated around to the people in Paradise.
1.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circumambulate; Form IV: to make go around, to circulate

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: With dishes, with platters — biṣiḥāfin is bi- (with) plus ṣiḥāf, the broken plural of ṣaḥfa (a large, flat dish or platter) in the indefinite genitive.

parts.en: plural noun (broken plural), indefinite genitive: dishes, platters, large bowls

3.grammar: Bi- governs the genitive. Ṣiḥāfin is the broken plural of ṣaḥfa in the indefinite genitive (-in tanwīn kasra). The genitive follows the preposition to form an adverbial: 'with platters (of food)'.
3.root: ص-ح-ف (ṣ-ḥ-f) — flat surface, dish; page, sheet (ṣaḥīfa = scroll/page)

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: Gold — the precious yellow metal 'dhahab'.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -in ending: the genitive case with nunation. This case commonly links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'bracelets of gold') or follows a preposition.
5.root: ذ-ه-ب (dh-h-b) — gold; (also 'to go')

6.meaning: And cups — wa-akwābin is wa- (and) plus akwāb, the broken plural of kawb (a drinking cup without handle or spout) in the indefinite genitive.

parts.en: plural noun (broken plural), indefinite genitive: cups, goblets (without handles)

6.grammar: Wa- coordinates with biṣiḥāfin. Akwābin is the broken plural of kawb in the indefinite genitive (-in tanwīn) following bi- (implied from the previous phrase). Kawb specifically describes a rounded cup without handle or spout.
6.root: ك-و-ب (k-w-b) — cup, goblet (without handle)

7.meaning: A linked phrase meaning 'and in it' / 'and therein' — joining what follows to a feminine singular thing and locating something within or inside it.
7.grammar: Built from the connector 'wa' (and), the preposition 'fī' (in/within), and the attached pronoun '-hā' meaning 'it' for a feminine singular noun. A preposition like 'fī' always puts its object in the genitive, and the pronoun '-hā' is that genitive object, so the whole reads 'and in it.'

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: Desires it, craves it — tashtahīhi is the Form VIII imperfect of ishtahā (to desire, to crave, to long for) plus -hi (it, third-person masculine singular object).

parts.en: Form VIII imperfect, 3rd person feminine singular: it (the soul) desires, craves

9.grammar: Tashtahī is Form VIII (ishtahā) imperfect, third-person feminine singular (ta- prefix; the subject is a feminine noun like nafs 'soul'). The -ī ending is the long vowel of this defective verb's imperfect. The object -hi refers to what is desired.
9.root: ش-ه-و (sh-h-w) — to desire, crave; desire, appetite (shahwa)

10.meaning: The souls / the selves — the inner persons, the seats of life, desire and will within human beings. Nafs can mean soul, self, or one's very being.
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case, typically marking the word as the subject or doer of its clause.
10.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath, living being

11.meaning: And delights — wataladhu is wa- (and) plus taladhu, the imperfect of ladhdhiya/ladhdha (Form I or Form V: to find pleasure, to delight in, to be pleasurable).

parts.en: imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular: it delights, it gives pleasure

11.grammar: Wataladhu: wa- coordinates. Taladhu is Form I imperfect of ladhdha (to be delightful), third-person feminine singular (ta- prefix, subject is feminine: alaʿyun 'eyes', or the pleasures). The root has a doubled final radical.
11.root: ل-ذ-ذ (l-dh-dh) — to be delightful, pleasurable; delight, pleasure

12.meaning: The eyes — al-aʿyunu is the definite nominative of aʿyun, the broken plural of ʿayn (eye).

parts.en: plural noun (broken plural), definite nominative: the eyes

12.grammar: Al-aʿyunu is in the nominative (-u ending) as a subject. Aʿyun is the broken plural of ʿayn (eye). The nominative -u plus the definite article: al-aʿyunu. Eyes delighting signals visual pleasure in Paradise.
12.root: ع-ي-ن (ʿ-y-n) — eye; spring of water; to see

13.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
13.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

14.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
14.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

15.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
15.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
15.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: And that; and that one. 'Tilka' is a demonstrative pointing to something distant or notable ('that' / 'those'), prefixed with 'and'. It singles out and draws attention to a thing set apart.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a feminine demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' or 'those'. As a demonstrative it is fixed in form (it does not change for case) and serves to point out and identify something at a distance.

2.meaning: The Garden — the lush, walled garden of bliss; by extension Paradise, the abode of eternal reward. The article presents it as the well-known Garden.
2.grammar: A singular feminine noun with the article 'al-'. The '-u' ending is nominative, the case for a subject or for the predicate after 'is' (e.g. '… is the Garden'). The root sense of concealment underlies it: a garden whose ground is hidden by foliage.
2.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover/conceal; garden

3.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
3.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

4.meaning: You were given it as an inheritance / made its heirs — a group was caused to inherit and take possession of something, expressed as a completed action done to 'you all', with 'it' as the thing inherited.
4.grammar: A past-tense passive, causative (Form IV) verb. The '-tum' subject suffix ('you all', masculine plural) is vowelled '-tumū' (with the long ū written by the wāw) to link to the following object pronoun; the attached '-hā' ('it/her') is the thing received. As a passive causative it means 'you were made to inherit it'.

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
5.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
5.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

6.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
6.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

7.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
7.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
1.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
2.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

3.meaning: Fruit / fruits — the edible produce of trees and plants, taken as a delight.
3.grammar: A feminine noun (with tā' marbūṭa), indefinite. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks the nominative case as indefinite ('a/some'), typically marking the word as the subject or as standing on its own.

4.meaning: 'Many, abundant, numerous' — describing something great in quantity or amount.
4.grammar: A feminine adjective ('abundant'). The '-at' marks feminine agreement; the final '-un' (nunation) is nominative and indefinite — it typically marks the word as a subject or as describing an indefinite noun ('many ___ ').
4.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

5.meaning: From it / from her — marking the starting point or source out of which something comes, referring to a feminine or grammatically-feminine thing.
5.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.
5.root: — (particle/preposition)

6.meaning: You eat — to consume food; addressed to a group, describing an ongoing or habitual action.
6.grammar: The ta- prefix plus the -ūna ending mark the subject as 'you (masculine plural)'. The full -ūna ending (with its final nūn intact) is the indicative mood, presenting the eating as a real, ongoing or habitual fact rather than something negated or made conditional.
6.root: أ-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — to eat, consume

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: Those who commit grave sins and crimes; wrongdoers who deliberately break Allah's law and cut themselves off in guilt. The word denotes hardened, culpable offenders, not those who err by accident.
2.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) of Form IV, made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it names a group as the object of a verb or the complement of a preposition, rather than the subject.
2.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or grave sin

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: ʿAdhāb — punishment, torment, suffering inflicted as a penalty; severe chastisement.
4.grammar: A noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word names painful punishment and torment.

5.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
5.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
5.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

6.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
6.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
6.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: Will it subside, will it be lessened — yufattaru is the imperfect passive (or active) of fattara meaning to lessen, slacken, abate, or grow less intense.

parts.en: Form II imperfect passive, 3rd person masculine singular: it will be lessened, it will subside, it will be slackened

2.grammar: Yufattaru is the Form II passive imperfect (yu- prefix ḍamma, -a on the root = passive), third-person masculine singular. Form II of fatara (to split, abate) means 'to cause to abate, to lessen'. Passive: the punishment is not caused to abate (from outside).
2.root: ف-ت-ر (f-t-r) — to abate, subside, grow slack; to lessen

3.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
3.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

4.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
4.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

5.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

6.meaning: (Will) despair, be in utter hopelessness — mublisūna is the active participle plural of ablasa (Form IV: to be in despair, to be hopeless, to be struck dumb with grief).

parts.en: active participle plural (Form IV), nominative: those in despair, the utterly hopeless

6.grammar: Mublisūna is Form IV (ablasa = to fall into utter hopelessness/despair) active participle, masculine plural nominative (-ūna). Form IV is the causative: ablasa means to become struck with despair. Functions as a predicate: 'they are in utter despair'.
6.root: ب-ل-س (b-l-s) — to be silent in despair; Form IV: to be in utter hopelessness, despair

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'We wronged them / We treated them unjustly' — a verb of doing injustice or oppression, with 'we' as the doer and 'them' as those wronged.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -nā ending means 'we' (the doers, completed action), and the attached -hum means 'them' as the object — 'we wronged them.'
2.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression

3.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
3.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

4.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
4.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

5.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
5.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

6.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
6.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.
6.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; wrongdoing, injustice

1.meaning: And they called out: a completed-action verb of summoning or hailing aloud, calling to someone at a distance or proclaiming a call.
1.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in Form III, which often carries the sense of doing something toward or at another party. The -aw ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The wa- prefix means 'and.'
1.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w/y) — to call out, summon, hail

2.meaning: O Malik! — yāmāliku is the vocative yā (O!) plus Mālik, a proper name meaning 'the Owner/King', which is the name of the guardian/keeper of Hell (Mālik, the angel in charge of Hell).

parts.en: proper noun, definite vocative: Malik (the guardian/keeper of Hell)

2.grammar: Yā is the vocative. Māliku is the vocative form of the proper name Mālik (nominative ending -u maintained in many vocative usages of proper names in Arabic). Mālik is the active participle of malaka (to own/rule), used as a proper name.
2.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule, possess; king, owner, possessor

3.meaning: Let him put an end (to us), let him cause (us) to die — liyaqḍi is li- (let, may) plus yaqḍi, the jussive imperfect of qaḍā meaning to decree, to finish, to put an end to, to cause death.

parts.en: jussive imperfect, 3rd person masculine singular: let him decree/end it, let him cause death

3.grammar: Li- here is the lām al-amr (commanding/optative lām) governing the jussive (majzūm) mood. Yaqḍi is the jussive of qaḍā (defective root: the final yāʾ drops in jussive: yaqḍī → yaqḍi). Together: 'let him put an end to us / let him cause our death'.
3.root: ق-ض-و/ي (q-ḍ-w/y) — to decree, finish, decide; to put an end to, to die

4.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
4.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

5.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
5.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, sustaining, mastery

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

7.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
7.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: Will remain, will abide — mākithūna is the active participle plural of makatha (to stay, to tarry, to abide, to remain for a long time) in the nominative.

parts.en: active participle plural, nominative: those who will remain, those who abide, the staying ones

8.grammar: Mākithūna is the Form I active participle (fāʿil pattern: mākthu- → mākithū) masculine plural nominative (-ūna). It describes the state of the inhabitants of Hell: 'you are those who will remain / you will indeed abide here'.
8.root: م-ك-ث (m-k-th) — to stay, remain, tarry, abide for a long time

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: We have brought you — jiʾnākum is the perfect verb jiʾnā (we came/brought, Form I first-person plural) plus -kum (you plural). Together: 'We have brought you (the truth)'.

parts.en: perfect verb, 1st person plural: We came to, We brought to

2.grammar: Jiʾnā is the Form I perfect, first-person plural (the -nā suffix). It comes from the irregular verb jāʾa (to come). The -kum is the second-person masculine plural pronoun as indirect object or beneficiary: 'We came to you / We brought you'.
2.root: ج-ي-أ / ج-و-أ (j-y-ʾ) — to come; to bring; coming

3.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
3.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

4.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
4.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

5.meaning: 'Most of you' / 'the greater number of you' — the comparative/elative noun 'greater part, majority' joined to the pronoun 'you all'. It denotes the larger portion of a group.
5.grammar: An elative noun (the 'most/greatest' form) with the suffixed pronoun -kum ('you', masculine plural) functioning like a possessive: 'the most of you.' The -a vowel before the pronoun is an accusative/object ending, the case typically taken when the word is the object of a verb or otherwise governed in that position.
5.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

6.meaning: 'To/for the truth' — al-ḥaqq is that which is real, true, established, and rightfully due: reality as it actually is, the right that is owed, and truth as opposed to falsehood. With the prefix it means 'to the truth' or 'for the truth'.

parts.en: truth / reality / what is rightfully due

6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to the definite noun al-ḥaqq ('the truth'). The -i ending is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition such as li-.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, real, established, rightfully due

7.meaning: An active participle (a doer-noun) meaning 'ones who dislike / are averse / find something hateful' — people who feel reluctance or aversion toward something.
7.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural, naming those who carry out the action: 'those who dislike'. The -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the nominative case, which is typically used for the subject or for a predicate describing the subject.
7.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — to dislike, be averse, find hateful

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: Have they determined, have they plotted — abramū is the third-person masculine plural perfect of abrama (Form IV of b-r-m: to twist firmly, to settle firmly, to decide/determine on a plan).

parts.en: Form IV perfect, 3rd person masculine plural: they have determined, they have firmly resolved, they have plotted

2.grammar: Abramū is Form IV (abrama) perfect, third-person masculine plural (the wāw suffix + dropped alif). Form IV of b-r-m means 'to twist firmly, to clinch (a decision), to firmly resolve'. Here: 'have they firmly decided on a plot?'.
2.root: ب-ر-م (b-r-m) — to twist firmly; Form IV: to settle firmly, determine, clinch a decision

3.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or thing to be done. It can mean an order issued or, more broadly, any business, situation, or decreed affair.
3.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with tanwīn (the -an ending), which marks it as indefinite and typically as the object of a verb ('a matter') or otherwise grammatically governed. The accusative shows it is being acted upon rather than acting.

4.meaning: Then indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis and a connecting 'then/so'. The particle inna strongly affirms the statement, while the prefix fa- ties it as a consequence to what came before.
4.grammar: The connective fa- ('then, so', often marking a result) prefixed to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly'), with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The whole emphatically asserts a statement about 'we' as a consequence.

5.meaning: (Are) determined, have firmly resolved — mubrimūna is the Form IV active participle plural of abrama (to determine firmly, to make an irreversible decision) in the nominative.

parts.en: active participle plural (Form IV), nominative: those who are determined, the firmly resolved

5.grammar: Mubrimūna is the Form IV active participle (mufʿilūn pattern) masculine plural nominative (-ūna). It describes those who have made a firm, irreversible decision. Functions as a predicate: 'We are those who are firmly determined'.
5.root: ب-ر-م (b-r-m) — to twist firmly; Form IV: to determine firmly, to settle irrevocably

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: 'They reckon / suppose / think' — to form an opinion or assume something to be the case; the verb also carries the sense of counting or calculating.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks 'they' (a masculine plural) as the doers: 'they reckon/suppose'. The retained -na is the sign of the plain indicative mood, used for a simple ongoing statement.
2.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — reckoning, counting, supposing

3.meaning: That We … — an emphatic linking particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'We.' 'Anna' introduces and asserts a fact ('that indeed …'), and the attached 'We' names the doer (a majestic or plural 'We').
3.grammar: An emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā 'we.' This family of particles takes a following noun/pronoun in the accusative as its subject, so -nā here functions as that subject: 'that We …'. It firmly introduces a stated fact.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: we hear / listen — the act of perceiving sound, or attending and giving ear to what is said.
5.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -u is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of present or future action ('we hear / we will hear').
5.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen, heed

6.meaning: Their secret: that which a group keeps hidden or concealed within themselves — a private matter, inner thought, or undisclosed intention belonging to them.
6.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -a on the stem is the accusative case marker, which typically flags the noun as the direct object of a verb. The attached -hum means 'their' (a group of males), so the whole is 'their secret'.
6.root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r) — to be secret/hidden; also delight (a hidden inner state)

7.meaning: And their private/confidential talk: a hushed conversation held aside, secret counsel or whispered exchange among people that excludes others.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The core word is a verbal noun for confidential talk; its ending here is the long ā (written with the dagger alif). The attached -hum means 'their' (a group of males): 'and their secret conversation'.
7.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to confide privately, hold secret counsel; also to be saved/escape

8.meaning: Yes indeed / nay, rather — an affirmative reply used specifically to contradict a preceding negative and assert the positive: 'Yes (it is so), on the contrary.'
8.grammar: A response particle. Unlike a plain 'yes', it is used to overturn a negative statement or question and affirm what was denied. It does not inflect; the final long '-ā' is part of its fixed form.
8.root: — (particle — no root)

9.meaning: And Our Messengers — warusulunā is wa- (and) plus rusul (the broken plural of rasūl: messengers, prophets) plus -nā (our, first-person plural possessive).

parts.en: plural noun (broken plural), nominative construct: messengers, prophets

9.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Rusulunā is the broken plural of rasūl in the nominative construct (rusulu- before -nā, dropping tanwīn for the possessive suffix). -Nā is the first-person plural (divine majestic we) possessive.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; messenger, envoy, prophet

10.meaning: In their presence / with them / by them — an adverb of place meaning 'at/by/near', fused with 'them' (a group of males), indicating proximity or possession.

parts.en: at / with / in the presence of

10.grammar: The locational word ladā ('at / with / in the presence of'), which shifts to the form laday- when a pronoun is attached, here -him ('them', a group of males). It indicates nearness, presence, or possession.

11.meaning: 'They write / inscribe' — a present-tense verb of writing: to record, inscribe, or set down in letters; it can also carry the broader sense of prescribing or decreeing.
11.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are writing.'
11.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing; recording, inscribing, prescribing

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
2.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

3.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

3.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

4.meaning: 'To / for the All-Merciful.' Al-Rahman is a divine name of Allah denoting the One whose mercy is vast, all-embracing, and overflowing to the whole of creation; the prefixed 'to/for' directs an action or dedication toward Him.
4.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('to / for'). Because li- demands the genitive case, the noun takes the final -i ending. The article al- assimilates into the following 'r' sound (heard as ar-Rahman). The form al-Rahman is an intensive pattern signifying overwhelming, all-encompassing mercy.

5.meaning: A son — waladun is the indefinite nominative of walad (child, offspring, son). In the context of Allah being attributed a son.

parts.en: noun, indefinite nominative: a son, a child, offspring

5.grammar: Waladun is in the indefinite nominative (-un tanwīn ḍamma). Walad can mean son, daughter, or offspring generally, though in context it refers to the false attribution of a son to Allah, which the Qur'an strongly refutes.
5.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, to beget; child, offspring, son

6.meaning: Then I — fa-anā is the connective fa- (then, so) plus anā (the first-person singular independent pronoun: I). Used to make a statement after a conditional or connective.
6.grammar: Fa- is the connective/consequential particle. Anā is the independent pronoun 'I', which is used for emphasis in Arabic when the verb already marks the person (the pronoun is added for stress). In a nominal sentence it functions as the subject.
6.root: — (anā is a personal pronoun; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in order, time, or rank. It marks the initial or leading member of a set.
7.grammar: A noun/adjective of the elative-type pattern 'afʿal' ('first'). The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('… is the first'). It identifies the foremost in sequence or standing.
7.root: ء-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to precede

8.meaning: Of the worshippers, of those who worship — al-ʿābidīna is the definite masculine plural oblique (genitive/accusative) of ʿābid (worshipper, one who worships), the Form I active participle of ʿabada.

parts.en: active participle plural (Form I), definite oblique: the worshippers, those who worship

8.grammar: Al-ʿābidīna is the masculine plural oblique (-īna ending) of the active participle ʿābid (one who worships). The oblique (genitive/accusative) follows prepositions (e.g., min al-ʿābidīna: 'of the worshippers').
8.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve; worshipper, devoted servant

1.meaning: An exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of every flaw, partner, or imperfection — 'Glory be! / How perfect He is!' It is a noun of glorification used to affirm absolute transcendence and purity.
1.grammar: A verbal noun in the accusative case, marked by the -a ending; it functions as an exclamation typically followed by a noun in the genitive ('Glory be to …'). It conveys the act of declaring someone free of any defect.
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; figuratively to declare free of imperfection

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
2.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

5.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
5.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

6.meaning: The Throne — the mighty seat of sovereignty and dominion. Literally a throne or canopy of a king; used as an image of supreme authority and rule.
6.grammar: A definite noun in the genitive case (the -i ending). The genitive appears when a noun follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun in a possessive 'X of Y' relationship. The l- prefix makes it definite ('the').
6.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — throne, canopy, seat of dominion

7.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
7.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

8.meaning: They describe, characterize, or ascribe (qualities to something) — to attribute traits or make claims about what a thing is like. It can carry the sense of falsely ascribing, depending on what is described.
8.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix with -ūna marks a masculine plural subject in a real, ongoing or habitual action: 'they describe / they attribute'. The final -na shows the full (indicative) form.
8.root: و-ص-ف (w-ṣ-f) — to describe, characterize, ascribe qualities

1.meaning: A command verb with an attached object, meaning 'so leave them / let them be / forsake them'. The underlying verb means to leave something alone, abandon it, or let it go.
1.grammar: fa- is 'so / then', drawing a consequence. dhar is an imperative (command) addressed to a single male ('you, leave!'); this very common verb is used only in present and command forms. The suffix -hum is the object 'them' (a group of males).
1.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, let alone, forsake

2.meaning: They plunge into or engage in (idle or vain talk); to wade into a discourse, often one of mockery or falsehood.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they plunge in / engage'). The ya- prefix marks third person and the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The final -na has been dropped (subjunctive/jussive), so it characteristically follows 'until', 'that', or a negation.
2.root: خ-و-ض (kh-w-ḍ) — to wade into water; to plunge into talk or affairs

3.meaning: And play, and let them play — wayalʿabū is wa- (and) plus yalʿabū, the jussive/subjunctive third-person masculine plural of laʿiba meaning to play, to be frivolous, to sport.

parts.en: jussive/subjunctive imperfect, 3rd person masculine plural: let them play, they may play

3.grammar: Wa- coordinates. Yalʿabū is the Form I imperfect in the jussive (after dharahum: 'leave them'), masculine plural dropping the -na: yalʿabūna → yalʿabū. The jussive mood follows the implicit command 'let them (be)'.
3.root: ل-ع-ب (l-ʿ-b) — to play, to sport, to be frivolous

4.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
4.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

5.meaning: They meet, they encounter — yulāqū is the Form III subjunctive/jussive of lāqā meaning to meet, to encounter, to come face to face with.

parts.en: Form III jussive/subjunctive, 3rd person masculine plural: they meet, they encounter (their day)

5.grammar: Yulāqū is Form III (lāqā — mufalāʿa: the reciprocal/intensive 'to meet') imperfect jussive, third-person masculine plural (dropping -na). The jussive follows ḥattā ('until') or similar governing particle. Form III of l-q-y means to meet face to face.
5.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter; Form III: to meet face to face

6.meaning: Their Day — yawmahumu is yawm (day) in the accusative construct plus -humu (their, third-person masculine plural pronoun). 'The Day belonging to them' = the Day of Judgment they will face.
6.grammar: Yawmahumu: yawm is in the accusative (construct, muḍāf, first term of iḍāfa). The -a ending is the accusative. -Humu is the third-person masculine plural pronoun suffix with a helping vowel -u (the full form before a following consonant cluster).
6.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day

7.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

8.meaning: 'They are promised / threatened' — something pledged to a group, whether a promised good or a warned-of consequence, with the group as recipient.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (the subjects receive the action). The yu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern signals 'are being …' (done to them). The -ūna ending marks 'they' (plural) in ongoing/repeated time.
8.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, warn of what is to come

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
4.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

5.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
5.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and in / and within.' It joins a new item to what precedes and places something inside or amid a sphere, time, or place.
6.grammar: A compound of the connector 'wa' (and) plus the preposition 'fī' (in). 'fī' governs a following noun, putting it in the genitive case and locating something inside it, whether in place, time, or situation.

7.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
7.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

8.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
8.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
8.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

9.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
9.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

10.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
10.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
10.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

11.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
11.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know

1.meaning: And blessed is, and exalted be — watabāraka is wa- (and) plus tabāraka, the Form VI (or Form V derived from bāraka) of baraka meaning to bless. Tabāraka is used exclusively of Allah and cannot be parsed as a normal verb — it conveys absolute, self-subsisting blessedness.

parts.en: verb (Form VI, exclusive to Allah): Blessed is He, Exalted in His blessedness

1.grammar: Tabāraka is grammatically a Form VI (tafāʿala) perfect, third-person masculine singular, but its meaning is unique: it expresses Allah's absolute, self-sufficient, ever-increasing blessedness. It is only ever used with Allah as its subject.
1.root: ب-ر-ك (b-r-k) — to bless, to abound in good; blessedness, blessing

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
3.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

4.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
4.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
4.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
5.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

6.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
6.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
6.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
7.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

8.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relation lying amid a pair.
8.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' fixed in the accusative as adverbs of place commonly are; the -a marks its adverbial function ('in the place that is between'). The attached -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
8.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

9.meaning: 'And with Him / in His possession' — 'ʿinda' means at, with, in the presence or keeping of someone, often implying ownership or that something rests in their hands; with the attached 'Him' it means 'with Him / in His possession'.

parts.en: with / in the presence or keeping of

9.grammar: An adverb of place/possession ('ʿinda', 'with/at') fixed in the accusative '-a' form, joined to the attached pronoun '-hu' ('him/his'). Together they express that something is in His presence or possession. Prefixed 'wa' means 'and'.
9.root: — (preposition/adverb; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: knowledge, knowing — sure awareness and understanding of something, the opposite of ignorance.
10.grammar: A noun meaning "knowledge." The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified; it also sets up a possessive link to a following noun ("the knowledge OF …").
10.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

11.meaning: The Hour — the appointed final time: the moment of the world's ending and the Resurrection. Though literally 'an hour' (a span of time), with the definite article it denotes that singular, decisive coming Hour.
11.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 's' (heard as 'as-sāʿa'). The final -i is genitive — the case used when the word is possessed by a preceding noun ('… of the Hour') or follows a preposition.
11.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a passing moment or span of time; an 'hour'

12.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
12.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

13.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
13.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: He owns / possesses / has power over — a verb meaning to have ownership, control, or authority over something, to be able to dispose of it as one wills.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a 3rd-person masculine singular subject ('he') and ongoing/future action. The final -u marks the indicative mood (a plain statement). The verb spans ownership, possession, and the power or authority to control and dispose of a thing.
2.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — ownership, dominion, possessing and holding sway

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They call / invite / summon' — to call upon, invite, or summon (also to pray to or call out to); a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
4.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('they do'), with its final nūn intact (contrast the jussive/subjunctive, where it drops).
4.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: Besides Him, other than Him — dūnihi is dūn (below, beside, apart from, other than) plus -hi (him/His). A common Qur'anic phrase meaning 'other than Allah / apart from Him'.

parts.en: adverb/preposition: below, beside, other than, apart from
3rd person masculine singular genitive: him, His

6.grammar: Dūni is a ẓarf (adverbial noun of place) in the genitive (following a preposition or in an iḍāfa). The suffix -hi is genitive. Together dūnihi means 'other than Him / besides Him / apart from Him'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — below, less than; beside, other than (relational particle)

7.meaning: 'Intercession' — the act of pleading or standing in on behalf of another, asking that they be pardoned or helped; a third party interceding to seek favor or relief for someone.
7.grammar: The al- means 'the' (here its l is assimilated into the following sh-, so it is pronounced ash-). The noun is in the accusative case, shown by the final -a, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb — the thing acted upon, such as what one possesses, owns, or controls.
7.root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ) — to pair, join, intercede on another's behalf

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
8.root: — (particle)

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
9.root: — (pronoun)

10.meaning: He witnessed, bore witness, or was present — to observe something directly and so be able to testify to it, or simply to be present for it.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular. The final -a marks a completed act done by 'he' ('he witnessed / was present').
10.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

11.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
11.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
11.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

12.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
12.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

13.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
13.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: To ask, question, or request — to put a query to someone or seek something from them. With the endings attached it means 'you asked them,' a completed act of questioning directed at a group.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person masculine singular ('you'); the further suffix -hum is the direct object 'them.'
2.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, question, request

3.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

4.meaning: He created them — a verb expressing the act of bringing a group into existence from nothing, with 'them' as the ones created.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb ('he created') with an attached object pronoun. The bare verb with -a is third-person masculine singular ('he'); the suffix -hum is the object 'them' (masculine plural). So: 'he created them.'

5.meaning: An emphatic assertion 'they will surely say / they will certainly say.' The word fuses an oath-like emphasis with a future statement of speaking, leaving no doubt that the utterance will occur. The heavy doubled ending drives home the certainty.
5.grammar: A present/future verb made doubly emphatic. The opening la- means 'surely'; the ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine subject; and the heavy -nna suffix (the 'energetic' ending) intensifies it to 'they will most certainly say.' Together la-…-nna is a fixed pattern of strong affirmation about something yet to happen.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
6.root: — (proper divine name)

7.meaning: An interrogative of manner or place meaning 'how?', 'in what way?', or 'whence / from where?'. It expresses wonder or challenge at how something could be so, often implying 'how on earth…?'.
7.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so/then') joined to an indeclinable question-word. Being a fixed particle, it has no case ending; it opens a question about manner or source and carries a tone of astonishment or rebuke.

8.meaning: They are turned away / deluded — a passive verb meaning that people are diverted away from truth toward falsehood, made to deviate from what is right.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice — the u- prefix vowel with an a-vowel on the stem signals 'are being [acted upon]', so the subjects are the ones turned away, not the ones turning. The -ūna ending marks a 3rd-person masculine plural subject ('they') and the indicative mood (a plain statement). The sense is being led astray or deluded away from the truth.
8.root: ا-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — turning away, deviation, falsehood and deception

1.meaning: And his saying, and what he said — waqīlihi is wa- (and) plus qīl (saying, speech, the thing said, report) plus -hi (his). Qīl is the verbal noun/noun of qāla (to say).

parts.en: noun (verbal noun: the saying, what was said), genitive construct

1.grammar: Waqīlihi: wa- coordinates. Qīli is the genitive construct (muḍāf) of qīl, the verbal noun meaning 'the saying, what was said'. In construct before -hi: 'and his saying / his words'. The genitive -i ending is marked on qīl.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; saying, speech, the thing said
